title: Enhancing the resilience of the gilt repo market – discussion paper feedback statement
summary: The Bank of England released a feedback statement summarizing industry responses to its September 2025 discussion paper on enhancing gilt repo market resilience. Respondents broadly supported the Bank's objective but opposed mandatory central clearing mandates or non-risk-sensitive minimum haircuts, citing access barriers, operational constraints, cost concerns, and procyclical margin risks. The Bank indicated it will explore incentive-based approaches to encourage voluntary adoption of central clearing and investigate how obstacles to greater clearing adoption could be overcome.
key_points: The gilt repo market has experienced structural changes: multinational leveraged hedge funds have increased participation while pension funds have become less active
Previous stress episodes (March 2020 'dash for cash', September 2022 LDI episode) demonstrated the need for improved market resilience

Respondents identified barriers to central clearing: existing access barriers, operational constraints, cost considerations, and limited balance sheet benefits due to dealer maturity transformation role
Most respondents opposed mandatory central clearing, instead favoring incentives such as cross-product margining, expanded collateral pools, and clearing of Bank's Short-Term Repo (STR) facility
Most respondents were not supportive of non-risk-sensitive minimum haircuts on non-centrally cleared repo, noting they would raise funding costs and potentially divert activity
Additional proposals included innovations to CNRF and Sterling Monetary Framework, less procyclical CCP margin models, and development of tri-party repo infrastructure
why_it_matters: The gilt repo market is critical infrastructure for UK financial stability, government cash management, and market-based funding. Structural vulnerabilities exposed during the 2020 and 2022 stress episodes could transmit disruptions to broader financial markets and the real economy. This feedback statement informs future regulatory design that could reshape how the gilt repo market operates, affecting dealers, hedge funds, pension funds, and the cost of government debt management.
market_structure_context: The document directly addresses gilt repo market structure, including: central clearing adoption barriers, counterparty risk management, settlement risks, multilateral netting benefits, procyclical CCP margin behavior, dealer balance sheet constraints, tri-party repo infrastructure, and the Contingent Non-Bank Financial Institutions Repo Facility (CNRF). The Bank is collaborating with FCA, HM Treasury, and UK Debt Management Office on potential reforms.
